main_text.l: LAMENTATIONES PROPHETÆ IEREMIÆ VARIIS Lyricorum versuum generibus expressæ.

l.i: URBS ante cœlu splendida ciuium Florente, cunctis altior urbibus, Qui sola nunc mœret relicta, Coniuge ceu viduata coniux?

main_text.l: Urbs ante victis Gentibus imperans Qui victa seruit? Qui patitur iugum, Iussisque victorem superbum Muneribus veneratur hostem?

l.i: Attrita seuis casibus ingemit, Ultusque acerbis fletibus obruit, Noctesque totas inquieta Nunc vigiles iterat querelas.
Nullus fideli pectore turbidis Rebus sodalis nunc colit anxiam. Ceu quum superbis illa quondam Diuitiis nituit decora.

page.notes: The running head "LAMENTATIONES" faintly visible above the ornament is show-through from the reverse side and is omitted. The word after "cœ" in line 1 ("cœlu") is doubtful and may be [?]; the line-1 reading "cœlu" is my best reading of the scan. "Noctesque totas" was read as "tot as" with a gap; the spacing is uncertain. "pectore" and "vigiles" are read from a worn impression. The italic/roman setting of stanzas 2 and 3 is uncertain from the scan; stanza 2 looks roman, stanzas 1, 3 and 4 look italic. The woodcut initial "U" is joined to "RBS" as "URBS". Greek and Hebrew: none.
